summary: Which stack items a Virus may be augmented onto rests on the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“A Virus may be augmented onto…”)’s own judgement calls. Caleb names spells (and spell tokens); the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“A Virus may be augmented onto…”) excludes triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes, and marks each exclusion "not sourced" and "Bena to rule".

sides.quote: The four ⚠ are judgement calls, not sourced answers. **Bena to rule** if any of
`STACK_VIRUS_HOSTS = { spell, spellUnit, spellToken }`. The ruling names spells

resolution: The rule states the engine's exclusions (apply.ts STACK_VIRUS_HOSTS), basis engine, confidence low; the positive host set stays in effects.virus.spell-host.which. Owner sign-off needed; nothing in print or the RAQ decides the four exclusions.

summary: Caleb says a spell carrying a Virus "gets erased on resolution". The owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“A Virus may be augmented onto…”) makes an exception for spell units, which enter play with the Virus as an augment instead, and says no ruling asks for it.

resolution: The rule states the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“A Virus may be augmented onto…”)’s exception, basis owner. Its reasoning: {Unstable} replaces a bin entry (owner ruling of 2026-08-22, “A token entering a ZONE is…”), and a resolving spell unit does not go to a bin. summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“ModPermission: an opt-in permission to apply…”) left open whether Rook's battle permission covers grafting. Rook's printed text says "augment".

sides.quote: 3. **Does it cover GRAFT?** Printed text says "augment", `doGraft` is deployment-only,
You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].

resolution: Printed text answers it (the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“an erased card goes to the…”): "If the printed text answers it, it is not a question"). The rule states that Rook does not permit grafting in battle. Graft 101 point 1 (grafting only in deployment) agrees.

summary: The RAQ fizzle thread records that Caleb is considering a change under which a graft effect resolves even when it has lost all its targets.

sides.quote: Caleb is considering change of ruling for graft-targeting-fizzle, so even if it loses all targets it will still happen.
> **A:** "**If effect loses ALL of its targets and wants to resolve.**"

resolution: A possible future change, not a ruling. The rule states the current answer (owner ruling of 2026-08-23, “An effect fizzles when it loses…”). Revisit if Caleb rules.

summary: The Amphivore thread says an unpayable multiplied cost means "you don't get the effect". The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“"Trigger two/three copies of this graft…”) read that as only that graft; Graft 101 point 11 says the whole graft effect stays off the stack, and the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“A grafted [cost] is mandatory, and…”) applies that to the multiplied case.

sides.quote: No Sacrifice at all and you don't get the effect.
if you can't pay it (no units to sacrifice) then the whole Graft Effect won't go on the stack.
This narrows R110. R110 skipped "that effect", meaning only the graft whose cost failed, and the engine treated grafted costs as opt-in riders. That opt-in was never backed by a ruling. Now:

resolution: Both are designer sources; Graft 101 point 11 is explicit and the Amphivore line fits it. The rule states the whole composite stays off the stack (owner ruling of 2026-10-09, “A grafted [cost] is mandatory, and…”). No owner question.

summary: Sources silent on a graft multiplier grafted under another multiplier (for example a Lost Guardian grafted under an Amphivore). The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“"Trigger two/three copies of this graft…”) calls it unruled.

summary: That Rook's permission works only in Rook's region rests on a player's chat remark, quoted in the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“ModPermission: an opt-in permission to apply…”). Players are not authority; Rook's printed text names no region.

sides.quote: the rules'. Region scoping is not a convenience either; on this exact card, rodanaw in
You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].
Yes everything in the game is region specific.

resolution: Settled by the designer for the region half (2026-10-25 search): Caleb, asked about Ghord, "Yes everything in the game is region specific. Just add 'in this region' to every card if it helps." (RAQ 1454169054402314362#0). Rook's permission is an effect of the game and is scoped to Rook's region like every other. effects.virus.permission.region now cites it, basis mixed. That the permission belongs to the grantor's controller is unchanged (owner).

summary: Graft 101 says grafting is done only in deployment, whatever the card's speed. Spellbind's printed {Modular} reminder and the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“{Modular} takes ANY mod you can…”) let any card, a graft card included, be applied to a Modular card as it is played, and Spellbind is a {Battle} card; the engine applies a graft card to Spellbind in battle.

sides.quote: Grafting can only be done during Deployment Phase
You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played.
> "I think it's legal to apply ANYTHING to a Modular card. But many cards wont

resolution: The specific printed permission wins over the general statement: Graft 101 is read as being about grafting onto a unit, and the rule lists Modular as an exception (722.3a). Question for the owner only if he reads Graft 101 as forbidding a graft card on Spellbind in battle.

summary: The Manual says flatly that a Virus in a bin cannot be used as a mod during battle; Rook lets cards from the bin be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses, and names no exception for a card that already is a Virus. The engine lets a bin Virus be augmented in battle under Rook (r2 verifier probe).

sides.quote: cannot be used as a mod during battle.
You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].

resolution: The card's specific permission is read as an exception to the Manual's general note, and the rule says so; the engine agrees. Question for the owner only if Rook's "as if they were [Virus]" is meant to reach only non-Virus cards.

summary: The RAQ write-up on Tides of the Cosmos (thread 1396955380000755795) was edited by _passer on 2026-08-14 to say "Having Rook would allow you to use Augments" (claim #4, recorded as outdated). Rook prints that it reaches cards "from hand and bin", and Tides plays cards off the top of the deck. No message by the designer says the edited line.

sides.quote: You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].
Having Rook would allow you to use Augments

resolution: The owner, 2026-10-25 (CT-390): "No (printed text)". The write-up's Rook line is not followed: Rook reaches the hand and the bin only, so Tides of the Cosmos applies only true Viruses, with or without Rook. effects.virus.permission.zones carries the call; the engine is unchanged.

summary: Whose erased pile a spell carrying a Virus, and the Virus itself, go to has no printed or designer source (CT-401). The owner's zones-follow-control calls name cards leaving play; the engine applies the same rule to a spell and its Virus leaving the stack: the spell to its caster's pile, the Virus to the pile of the player who applied it.

sides.quote: Zones ALWAYS follow control. One rule, no split.
(a) All four follow control

resolution: Stated as the owner's rule extended to the stack (effects.virus.spell-host.erased-piles), as the engine does (89). Awaits the owner's sign-off for the stack case.
